outcome: No resolution, partial resolution, or scope-qualifying bound improvement was found since 26 January 2024; the Maass-form and general automorphic generalizations remain open, and the one long-running claimed proof for Maass forms of SL(2,Z) remains an unaccepted, undigested preprint.
summary: The Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture (for modular forms) was proved by Deligne in the 1970s; the bullet as given is the umbrella statement covering the still-open generalizations (Maass forms of SL(2,Z), and general automorphic forms on higher-rank groups). I checked the current Wikipedia article, which explicitly states 'As of 2025, the version of the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for Maass forms is still open' and that the automorphic-forms generalization also remains open — no post-2024 resolution is recorded there. The one item the triage flagged, André Unterberger's single-author arXiv preprint 2001.10956 ('The Ramanujan-Petersson and Selberg conjectures for Maass forms'), was first posted 29 Jan 2020 — before the window — and has been revised 16 times through v16 (12 Feb 2026), including two withdrawals (v2, v5) along the way. This long, contested revision history with no journal acceptance and no expert digestion found anywhere (no citation of it as settling the question in surveys, blogs, or subsequent literature) means it does not establish a change in status; per the resolved-vs-claimed rule, even 'claimed' would require the paper to still be a live, credible claim, and a 6-year unaccepted single-author preprint repeatedly withdrawn and rewritten does not meet that bar for either 'claimed' or 'resolved' — so the correct call is that the conjecture is still `open`, with this preprint noted but not counted. I searched for other results that might qualify as scope-appropriate progress (a case settled or a genuine bound improvement toward the generalized Ramanujan conjecture at pointwise/individual coefficient level, per Kim-Sarnak-style bounds). I found: (1) Yujiao Jiang's July 2025 preprint (2507.20653) proving 'Hypothesis H of Rudnick and Sarnak' for GL(n) over any number field in full generality — but this is an average/Euler-product statement about Rankin-Selberg coefficients, not a pointwise Ramanujan-type bound on individual Satake parameters, so it is a related-but-distinct statement (a 'related problem' under §3.1), not a case of this conjecture; (2) Liyang Yang's improvement to the Kim-Sarnak 7/64 bound for exceptional Maass forms, which is genuine bound-moving progress in scope, but the paper (arXiv:2011.09054) was first posted 18 November 2020 -- also before the window, so it is not a post-2024 event, whatever its later revision history; (3) Yuhao Cheng's 2025-2026 paper (arXiv:2507.09655) on 'Beyond Endoscopy for GL2 with ramification 2', which gives a *new proof* of the already-known 1/4 bound in a ramified case -- a new derivation, not a numerically improved bound, so it does not change what a careful person would write in this bullet. I also searched explicitly for any AI-system involvement (deep learning, LLM-driven proof search, AlphaProof/AlphaEvolve, or the 'Ramanujan Machine') in connection with this conjecture; the only AI-adjacent hits were the unrelated 'Ramanujan Machine' project (generates numerical conjectures for constants like pi, e) and its 2026 'Ramanujan Challenge for AI' benchmark paper, and AlphaEvolve's unrelated work on Ramanujan *graphs* (expander graphs, a different structure sharing only the name). None of these touch the Ramanujan-Petersson conjecture for automorphic/Maass forms. No AI system appears anywhere near this specific problem.
competing_reading: If a reader takes the Unterberger preprint's persistence and continued revision (through Feb 2026) as evidence of a live, increasingly refined claim rather than a stalled one, they might classify this as `claimed` with event dated to the most recent substantive revision. I do not take this reading because there is no evidence any expert has endorsed or even seriously engaged with the claim in six years, and repeated withdrawals (v2, v5) are a signal of substantive problems rather than routine polishing.
what_would_settle_it: A citation of Unterberger's paper by an independent expert (survey, seminar report, or journal referee) treating it as correct or substantively reviewed, or a journal acceptance, would move it to `claimed` or `resolved`. Absent that, continued arXiv-only revision does not count as movement.
